headline: This law lets the Treasury Department mint commemorative coins honoring the 100th anniversary of the Negro National League, with sale surcharges going to the Negro Leagues Baseball Museum.
what_it_does: The law directs the Treasury Department to mint and issue up to 50,000 five-dollar gold coins, 400,000 one-dollar silver coins, and 400,000 half-dollar clad coins. The coins mark the 100th anniversary of the Negro National League, a professional baseball league formed after Black players were barred from the major leagues. Treasury may issue them only during a one-year period starting January 1, 2022, and all surcharges from sales go to the Negro Leagues Baseball Museum for education and exhibits. Treasury must also run a program to promote coin collecting.

who_it_affects.how: People can buy these limited-edition coins during the one-year sales window, at prices that include a surcharge.
The museum receives the surcharges from coin sales to fund its educational programs, outreach, and exhibits.
Treasury must produce the coins within the set limits and run a marketing and educational program to promote them.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted December 4, 2020, and Treasury may issue the coins only during the one-year period beginning January 1, 2022.
